 ETUDE’s Global Marketing Head on India’s growing K-beauty opportunity
 As K-beauty gains a stronger foothold in India's beauty market, Global Head of Marketing at ETUDE discusses the brand's India strategy and the opportunities shaping the category. 
 Sneha Medda 
 20 Nov 2026 
 18:11
 IST Follow Us
 New Update From K-pop fandoms and K-drama watch parties to food, fashion and skincare routines, the Korean Wave has steadily found its way into India's pop-culture. What began as an interest in Korean entertainment has gradually evolved into a larger lifestyle influence, with beauty emerging as one of its most visible extensions.  
 The influence has translated into a growing appetite for Korean beauty products, formulations and techniques. India's K-beauty market is projected to reach $1.5 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 25.9%. The India K-Beauty Products Market reached a value of INR 3,139.31 crore in 2025 and is projected to grow at a CAGR of approximately 26.30% between 2026 and 2035. And the number of K-beauty consumers in the country is also expected to rise from 11.9 million to 27.2 million by 2030. 
 However, the K-beauty influence is no longer limited to consumers picking up products from Korean labels. Its impact is increasingly visible in the Indian beauty industry's own product development. From cushion foundations and lightweight, dewy base products to lip tints, hydrating formulations and evolving sunscreen textures, beauty brands in India are beginning to experiment with formats and product experiences that have long been associated with Korean beauty.  
 For Korean beauty brands, this growing interest also brings the opportunity to move beyond being a part of a larger cultural trend and establish a more enduring presence in the Indian market.  
 ETUDE, which entered India in April 2019 through a partnership with Nykaa, is looking to build on this opportunity. Having initially built recognition among Indian consumers through its lip products, the Korean brand is now looking to deepen that relationship by entering the complexion category with its Double Lasting Foundation and Powder Cushion. 
 As it looks to expand its footprint in India, the brand's focus is shifting towards strengthening consumer preference, encouraging repeat purchases and building a more sustainable growth strategy. Soye Cho , Global Head of Marketing, ETUDE , discusses the brand's evolving India strategy, the growing influence of K-beauty on local product preferences, and how it plans to carve out a distinct space in the market. 
 Edited Excerpts:  
 Q. ETUDE is entering the foundations category in India at a time when the beauty market is seeing growing interest in complexion products and more diverse makeup routines. What informed the timing of this launch, and how does the category fit into the brand’s larger growth strategy for India? Why was the festive period chosen, and how important is it for ETUDE in India? 
 We see complexion as a natural next step in the brand’s journey in India. Our lip products have introduced many consumers to the brand, and expanding into foundation allows us to connect with them through another important part of their makeup routine. 
 The timing is particularly relevant because consumers are exploring more diverse makeup looks and paying greater attention to complexion, coverage and finish. With our Double Lasting Foundation and Powder Cushion, we want to bring ETUDE’s makeup expertise to consumers who are looking for products that complement their individual preferences. 
 The festive period also presents a meaningful opportunity in India. Beauty becomes an important part of celebrations, weddings and social occasions, and consumers are often more open to experimenting with their looks. Launching during this time allows us to introduce the category when makeup is especially relevant to consumers. 
 For us, this is not just a seasonal opportunity. It is part of our larger ambition to build a stronger presence in India and expand the ways in which consumers experience the brand. 
 Q. How do you plan on marketing this product in the market? Which channel gets the highest budgets? 
 Our approach is to build awareness while also helping consumers understand the product and make informed choices. Foundation is a category where the right shade, finish and application experience matter, so simply creating visibility is not enough. 
 We see creator-led content as an important way to demonstrate the product in real-life settings, show application techniques and help consumers understand how it looks on different people. Digital beauty platforms also provide an opportunity to communicate product benefits and support the purchase journey. 
 View this post on Instagram Alongside digital marketing, we believe in the value of product trials and interactive experiences wherever possible. These can help consumers feel more confident about exploring a new complexion product. 
 In terms of budget allocation, our investments are guided by the campaign objective, the consumer we want to reach and the effectiveness of each channel. Rather than viewing one channel in isolation, we aim to create a connected journey from discovery to consideration and purchase. 
 Q. K-beauty has moved from being a niche interest to a more visible part of India’s beauty market. From ETUDE’s global perspective, how has the opportunity in India evolved, and what changes have you observed in the way Indian consumers discover, evaluate and purchase Korean beauty products? 
 India has become an increasingly interesting market for Korean beauty because consumers are more connected to global trends and have greater access to international beauty brands than ever before. 
 What is changing is the depth of consumer engagement. Discovery may begin with a social media video, a creator recommendation or an interest in Korean culture, but consumers are increasingly looking for more information before making a purchase. They want to understand product performance, textures, shades and how a product fits into their own routine. 
 This creates an opportunity for brands like ours to go beyond trend-led awareness and build stronger consumer relationships through product education and a distinctive brand experience. 
 From our perspective, India's opportunity lies not just in attracting new consumers to K-beauty, but in building long-term engagement as consumers become more familiar with the category. 
 Q. As K-beauty becomes more mainstream, what does it take for a Korean beauty brand to stand out beyond the appeal of its country of origin? How is ETUDE thinking about building a distinct brand identity in a market where more Korean brands are competing for consumer attention? 
 Korean origin can create curiosity, but a brand needs a much stronger reason for consumers to keep coming back. 
 We have always approached beauty through colour, creativity, playfulness and self-expression. We want makeup to feel enjoyable and accessible, giving consumers the freedom to experiment rather than follow a single definition of beauty. 
 Our product heritage, particularly in lip tints and colour cosmetics, is an important part of that identity. As we expand into categories such as complexion, we want to carry the same spirit into every product we introduce. 
 Ultimately, our ambition is for consumers to recognise the brand not only as a Korean beauty brand, but as a brand with its own point of view and a meaningful place in their beauty routines. 
 Q. How much of ETUDE’s global brand strategy can be carried into India, and where does the market require a more localised approach? Could you share examples of how Indian consumer insights have influenced campaign messaging, product communication or market execution? 
 Our global brand identity is the foundation of everything we do. The playful spirit of ETUDE, our emphasis on colour and our belief in self-expression remain consistent across markets. 
 However, how we bring that identity to life needs to reflect the consumers we are speaking to. India has a distinctive beauty calendar, a wide range of skin tones and preferences, and cultural occasions that influence how and when consumers engage with makeup. 
 For example, the festive and wedding seasons create opportunities to communicate makeup through celebration, occasion-led looks and self-expression. For a foundation launch, we also need to place greater emphasis on shade selection, product finish and application education so consumers can make informed choices. 
 We believe effective localisation is about making the global brand more relevant without losing what makes it distinctive. It is a balance between consistency in our identity and flexibility in how we communicate it. 
 Q. Beauty discovery is increasingly shaped by creators, short-form video, online reviews and peer recommendations. How is ETUDE approaching creator-led marketing in India, and what determines the kind of creators or content formats the brand chooses to work with? 
 Creators play an important role because beauty is a highly visual and personal category. Consumers want to see how a product looks, how it is applied and how it performs beyond a studio image or product description. 
 Our approach is to identify creators whose content, audience and style align with the product and the message we want to communicate. We also look at how naturally they can demonstrate the product and explain its benefits in a way that feels relatable to their audience. 
 Different formats serve different purposes. Short-form videos can introduce a product quickly, while tutorials, wear demonstrations and detailed reviews can help consumers evaluate it more carefully.

 For a complexion product, for example, showing shade selection and application can be especially useful. We want creator partnerships to do more than generate visibility; they should help consumers understand the product and feel more confident about trying it. 
 View this post on Instagram 
 Q. India’s beauty market spans consumers with very different budgets, beauty routines and levels of familiarity with Korean products. How does ETUDE identify and prioritise its target audiences, and how might its messaging differ between existing K-beauty enthusiasts and consumers discovering the category for the first time, especially in regional markets? 
 We recognise that India is not one uniform beauty market. Consumers differ in their familiarity with K-beauty, their product preferences, their spending priorities and the way they discover brands. 
 For consumers who already know Korean beauty, the conversation can focus more on product innovation, textures, finishes and how a new product fits into their existing routine. 
 For consumers discovering our brand for the first time, we need to introduce the brand more clearly: what we stand for, what makes our products distinctive and how they can incorporate them into their everyday makeup routines. 
 As we look beyond major metropolitan markets, accessibility and education become particularly important. Digital platforms and creators can help bridge the discovery gap, while clear product information can make the purchase decision easier. 
 Our objective is to meet consumers at different stages of their beauty journey rather than communicate to everyone in the same way. 
 Q. What are the key marketing priorities for ETUDE in India over the next 12 months? How will the brand balance building overall brand awareness with driving consideration and sales for specific categories such as foundations? 
 Our focus is on strengthening ETUDE’s overall brand presence while making our expanded product portfolio more visible and relevant to Indian consumers. 
 At the brand level, we want more consumers to understand what we stand for: playful beauty, colour and self-expression. At the category level, we want to help consumers understand our products, their benefits and the different ways they can be used. 
 The foundation launch is an important opportunity to build on our existing recognition in lip products and introduce the brand to consumers who may be looking for complexion solutions. 
 We see these objectives as connected rather than separate. Strong brand awareness creates familiarity, while relevant content, product education and the right consumer experiences help translate that familiarity into consideration and purchase. 
 Over the coming year, our priority is to build that connection more effectively and ensure our marketing supports both brand development and sustainable business growth. 
 Q. Looking ahead, what would success in India look like for ETUDE over the next three to five years? Which categories, consumer segments or areas of brand building will be important to achieving that ambition? 
 For us, success would mean building ETUDE into a recognised and trusted beauty brand in India, with a strong consumer community and a portfolio that remains relevant as beauty preferences evolve. We want to build on our strength in lip products while developing categories such as complexion and exploring other opportunities that align with consumer needs. 
 Reaching more consumers beyond the largest metropolitan markets will also be important. As access to global beauty expands, we see an opportunity to connect with consumers at different stages of their beauty journey through relevant products, accessible education and engaging brand experiences. 
 Just as importantly, we want to build lasting relationships rather than depend only on individual trends or launches. Over the next three to five years, our ambition is to strengthen brand preference, encourage repeat engagement and create a sustainable foundation for ETUDE’s long-term growth in India.
